Note::unique¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signatures¶

Note Note::unique() const
Note Note::unique(std::int64_t dim) const

Return Sorted Distinct Values Or Slices¶

The two overloads answer related but different questions. unique() flattens all cells, removes repeated byte-identical values, sorts the survivors, and returns a rank-one Note. unique(dim) treats each complete slice along dim as one record, removes duplicate slices, sorts those slices lexicographically, and preserves the receiver’s rank and every other extent.

For a matrix, unique(0) compares whole rows and unique(1) compares whole columns. Two slices are equal only when every corresponding cell contains the same bytes. Slice ordering compares their cells in row-major sequence until the first difference. An explicit negative axis is normalized, so unique(-1) means distinct slices along the last axis; unlike the no-argument form, it does not flatten.

The result shares the packed text arena and creates new span metadata, avoiding cell-byte copies. Text and bytes modes are both supported and preserved. Undefined input remains undefined. unique() on a scalar returns a rank-one singleton, while unique(dim) on a scalar rejects because a scalar has no axis.

Empty slices have precise set semantics. If the selected axis has entries but another extent makes every slice empty, all those slices compare equal and one survives. If the selected axis itself has length zero, no slice survives and the original zero extent remains zero.

Example 1: Flatten, Sort, And Remove Repeats¶

const auto rows = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"b", "2", "a", "1", "b", "2"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{3, 2});
std::cout << "flattened\n" << pluss::note::print(rows.unique()) << '\n';

Output¶

flattened
Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["1", "2", "a", "b"]

The matrix shape is intentionally gone in this overload.

Example 2: Compare Whole Rows¶

const auto rows = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"b", "2", "a", "1", "b", "2"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{3, 2});
std::cout << "whole rows\n" << pluss::note::print(rows.unique(0)) << '\n';

Output¶

whole rows
Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "1"], 
  ["b", "2"]
]

The repeated row ["b", "2"] appears once, after the lexicographically smaller row.

Example 3: Compare Whole Columns With -1¶

const auto columns = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"b", "a", "b", "2", "1", "2"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 3});
std::cout << "whole columns\n"
          << pluss::note::print(columns.unique(-1)) << '\n';

Output¶

whole columns
Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b"], 
  ["1", "2"]
]

Columns ["b", "2"], ["a", "1"], ["b", "2"] become the two sorted columns ["a", "1"], ["b", "2"].

Example 4: Equal Empty Slices Collapse To One¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{2, 3, 0});
std::cout << "three equal empty slices\n"
          << pluss::note::print(empty.unique(1)) << '\n';

Output¶

three equal empty slices
Note(shape=[2, 1, 0], dim=3, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

Example 5: An Empty Selected Axis Stays Empty¶

const auto empty_axis = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{0, 2});
std::cout << "empty selected axis\n"
          << pluss::note::print(empty_axis.unique(0)) << '\n';

Output¶

empty selected axis
Note(shape=[0, 2], dim=2, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

Example 6: Scalar Flattening Adds A Rank-One Axis¶

std::cout << "scalar flattened\n"
          << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::make("x").unique()) << '\n';

Output¶

scalar flattened
Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["x"]

Example 7: Bytes Mode Is Preserved¶

const auto raw = pluss::note::bytes(
    std::vector<std::string>{"b", "a", "b"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{3});
std::cout << "raw bytes\n" << pluss::note::print(raw.unique()) << '\n';

Output¶

raw bytes
Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=bytes)
[b"a", b"b"]

Example 8: Absence Propagates But A Scalar Axis Rejects¶

try { (void)pluss::note::make("x").unique(0); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "unique scalar axis: rejected\n"; }
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "undefined unique defined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().unique().defined() << '\n';

Output¶

unique scalar axis: rejected
undefined unique defined=false

See Also¶

  • deduplicate: retain first-seen order instead of sorting.

  • sort: order lanes without removing repeated cells.

  • flatten: flatten while retaining every cell.
